text:
Marathon Petroleum rallied 3.4% today, reversing a brutal two-week slide, after oil prices ticked up and geopolitical tension around Iran showed signs of easing. Trump's comments on Monday that the Iran conflict would end "fairly soon" had briefly tanked crude—Brent dipped below $90—but today's recovery suggests traders are pricing in a more measured view: continued uncertainty rather than imminent peace. US crude sits at $99.64 and refineries are running hot at 94.5% capacity, which supports refiner margins when oil supplies are tight and product demand holds.

The stock had cratered over two weeks amid broad Iran-related oil volatility, swinging from hopes of a deal to skepticism (Rubio saying negotiations remain unproductive). Today's bounce reflects relief that the worst geopolitical fears have not materialized, rather than any single new catalyst.
